title: fix: serve public model stats from an hourly Tinybird snapshot
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Split from #16497, which now contains the 30-minute model-health cache. This PR changes only public model statistics.
- Compute seven-day stats once per hour in a Tinybird COPY snapshot, then serve them from a small table. Keep median prices, agent-run costs, private-model visibility, and the public response format.
- Tinybird-only: gen keeps its one-hour KV cache, so there is no Worker change and no deploy order. Prices can be up to ~2 h old; they are seven-day medians.
- Fixes the hourly vCPU 429s: when the KV key expires, 70–98 locations refresh in the same minute. Each refresh costs 2.7 CPU-s today, ~250 CPU-s against the 180 CPU-s/min budget. With the snapshot each refresh is a small table read. All 74 minutes with 429s in the last seven days were this refresh.
- Also covers callers outside our Workers (~40% of calls, e.g. Facebook's link crawler), which hit the public endpoint directly.

**Deploy (Tinybird, staging then prod):** `deployment create --check` passes against prod: 1 new datasource, 1 new copy pipe, 1 modified endpoint, no deletions. The deployment copies no data, so run `public_model_stats_refresh` before promoting, or the endpoint returns an empty list that gen caches for an hour. Then compare model counts and a few prices with the old endpoint.

gist.headline: Stats without the stampede
gist.blurb: The public model-stats endpoint gets an hourly snapshot instead of making dozens of locations recalculate the same seven-day numbers at once. Even link crawlers get a quieter path to the data.
gist.summary: Public model stats move to an hourly Tinybird snapshot of seven-day medians, replacing expensive calculations on cache refresh while preserving median prices, agent-run costs, private-model visibility, and the response format.
gist.impact: When the existing one-hour KV cache expires, 70–98 locations can read the small snapshot table instead of triggering the CPU spikes behind 74 minutes of 429s in the past week; direct callers benefit too, with prices potentially up to about two hours old.
